summary: Frontend-only test of dark-mode bug fix + regression suite for Jaleter Expo app. Reproduced a CRITICAL crash: NetWorthScreen (and LegacyScreen) referenced `t.pageBg` without ever calling `useThemed()`, causing a red-screen 'ReferenceError: t is not defined' the moment the user navigated to Net Worth or Legacy in ANY mode (light or dark). Fixed by adding `const t = useThemed();` at the top of both components. After fix, the full dark-mode acceptance flow passes: Welcome->Onboarding->Signup->Connect->Paywall->App->More->Settings->Dark. Shell background reports rgb(17,17,15) (=#11110f) on Home, Budget, Transactions, NetWorth, More, Settings, Legacy after selecting Dark. Toggling Light restores rgb(250,248,243) (=#faf8f3 cream) across all screens. Regressions pass: onboarding flow, budget-cat-give expand, tx-add opens sheet + tx-save works, nw-eye toggle hides values with '••••••'. Two minor visual issues remain: `cashProtection` card on Net Worth and `assumptionsCard` on Legacy are still hard-coded cream and do NOT invert in dark mode, so they appear as bright cream panels on the near-black page. Also noted React Native deprecation warnings for shadow* props and props.pointerEvents.

'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' warning from RN web. Search for pointerEvents={...} usage in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx.

rca_of_issue: RCA: When the main agent added dark-mode support via a ThemeCtx + `useThemed()` helper, it wired `t = useThemed()` into most screen components but missed two: NetWorthScreen (line 498) and LegacyScreen (line 557). Both bodies referenced `t.pageBg` on their ScrollView, but no `t` existed in scope, so JS threw ReferenceError as soon as React tried to render either screen (any mode, not just dark). Reproduction: open the app, onboard through to /app, tap 'Net Worth' bottom-nav or 'Your Legacy' from More → LogBox red screen. Mitigation applied: added `const t = useThemed();` as the first line inside each component. Verified via full playwright flow that Net Worth and Legacy now render cleanly and dark mode propagates to shell (#11110f) across every tab.
